papers.title: The Complete Two-Weight Z/5Z Goemans–Linial Cone
papers.problem_definition: Proof of the frozen original statement. For every real a,b >= 0 with a+b > 0, SDP_GL(G_{a,b}) = psi(G_{a,b}) = 5*min(a+2*b,2*a+b)/(6*(a+b)). Regarding cuts as unordered bipartitions and working up to the dihedral action, the optimal cuts are exactly the adjacent-pair orbit when a>b (including b=0), exactly the difference-two-pair orbit when b>a (including a=0), and every nontrivial cut when a=b>0. Modulo positive scaling, the nonzero optimal translation-invariant GL-feasible semimetrics are exactly v=2u when a>b, exactly u=2v when b>a, and every u,v>0 satisfying u<=2v and v<=2u when a=b>0. Translation averaging preserves squared-Euclidean realizability, all triangle inequalities, N, and D, so no non-translation-invariant feasible semimetric has a smaller objective.

papers.title: Time-Eight Positive-Sojourn Classification for Arbitrary Two-State Unitary Coins

papers.title: Fixed Sticky Refreshing Preserves the Exponent-Two Degree Laws in Range-Renewal Networks
papers.problem_definition: Proof of the frozen original statement. Let pi=(pi_i) be a nonincreasing strictly positive probability mass function with pi_k in RV_{-1/gamma} for some 0<gamma<1. Form the directed and undirected loop-deleted simple graphs from consecutive observations, suppress repeated edges, and normalize degree counts by the observed range as in source.md and problem.md. Then, almost surely, simultaneously for every fixed integer k>=1, the four clock-time limits of the directed and undirected degree-k masses and degree-at-least-k tails equal the corresponding iid limits. Taking k to infinity only after each clock-time limit, the directed and undirected tails are asymptotic to pi_k^gamma and 2^gamma pi_k^gamma, respectively, while the directed and undirected local masses are asymptotic to pi_k^gamma/k and 2^gamma pi_k^gamma/k, respectively. No simultaneous k=k(n) limit or uniform rho-to-one assertion is included.

papers.title: Local rigidity of component-triangle Cayley deformations at order-seven permutation Euler points
papers.problem_definition: Let P be any unsigned 7 by 7 permutation matrix having exactly one diagonal 1, exactly one antidiagonal 1, and no eigenvalue -1. Then P has cycle type 1+3+3. The origin is an isolated real common zero of D(Q)-1 and A(Q)-1 in this affine three-coordinate family. Consequently, no nonconstant real-continuous solution germ passes through the anchor, and no rational parametrization defined over R can map a real parameter value to the anchor while parametrizing nearby Euler points. papers.title: Minimum Shift-Equivalence Lag for the 2 × 2 k = 11 Baker Pair: A Partial Result on Strong Shift Equivalence
papers.problem_definition: Let A=[[1,12],[11,1]] and B=[[1,132],[1,1]]. If L>=1 and R,S are 2-by-2 matrices over the nonnegative integers satisfying AR=RB, SA=BS, RS=A^L, and SR=B^L, then L>=22. Such R,S exist at L=22, so 22 is the minimum lag within this precisely delimited 2-by-2 class. Consequently every strong-shift-equivalence chain from A to B, if one exists, has at least 22 elementary steps, because an m-step chain composes to a 2-by-2 shift equivalence of lag m. This does not settle whether any such unrestricted chain exists.

papers.title: A Four-Job Counterexample to an Almost-Exact Fathoming Rule for Job Sequencing and Tool Switching
papers.problem_definition: The universal claim in source.md is false. For n=m=4, c=3, T_1={1}, T_2={1,2}, T_3={1,3,4}, and T_4={2,3,4}, the unique maximizing unordered PI root pair is {1,4} and the unique next selected job is 3. If the root orientation is (1,4), the generated proper node (3,1,4) is fathomed under its unique KTNS history and has globally optimal completion (2,3,1,4). If the root orientation is (4,1), the generated proper node (4,3,1) is fathomed under its unique KTNS history and has globally optimal completion (2,4,3,1). The remaining job 2 is not covered by any node configuration in either case, so the Section 6.2 completion-pruning condition does not apply. Thus, under either reversal-symmetry orientation, an unsafe node exists with four jobs.

papers.title: Polynomial Solvability of a Two-Machine Unit-Time Resource-Constrained Job Shop with at Most Three Operations per Job

papers.title: Exact Encoding Ladders for a Uniform Bandwidth Law with an Endpoint Atom

The claim is only for the frozen uniform-plus-endpoint-atom law and not for general atomic bandwidth distributions.

papers.title: A Four-Dimensional Witness for the Modular-Balance Gap

papers.title: An Every-Order Bipyramid Disproof for S₂,₁,₁ ⊔ K₂ in Maximal Planar Graphs

papers.title: Maximal sorting time under clumped-letter insertion in two short multiplicity profiles
papers.problem_definition: Let phi be the greedy aba-avoiding stack map, and let T be its sorting time. For every integer r>=3, let q be any word using exactly r letters, each occurring twice except that at most one letter may occur three times. There is no bound on |A| or on those block multiplicities. Then T(W)=r if and only if T(q)=r. The proof uses a complete 28,800-input computer-assisted base at r=3 and induction on r. In particular, for every run-free q on r>=3 letters, each occurring at least twice, with 2r<=|q|<=2r+1, and every new terminal letter x, T(qx)=r iff T(q)=r. This proves the original first-letter deletion bridge for k>=4; it does not provide the requested complete uniform classification or enumeration M_k of length-2k+2 inputs.

papers.title: A bijection for 312/321-avoiding permutations whose cubes avoid 2143
papers.problem_definition: For every integer n>=0, let B_n be the permutations pi of [n] avoiding classical patterns 312 and 321 whose third compositional power pi^3 avoids 2143; no condition is imposed on pi^2. Let C_n be the ordered compositions of n with at most one part outside {1,3}, with one empty object in each set at n=0. Writing epsilon_d=(2,3,...,d,1), with epsilon_1=(1), the direct-sum map F(d_1,...,d_m)=epsilon_{d_1} direct-sum ... direct-sum epsilon_{d_m} restricts to a size-preserving bijection C_n -> B_n. Its inverse repeatedly records the position d of the minimum, removes the forced prefix epsilon_d, and subtracts d from the suffix. For every finite list of positive parts, F(d)^3 avoids 2143 if and only if at most one part is outside {1,3}. papers.title: The NNE distribution on Fuss–Catalan paths with a fixed number of peaks
papers.problem_definition: For every pair of integers m>=2,n>=1 and every integer 1<=k<=n, let W^(m)_(n,k)(t) sum t^nne(D) over all N=(0,1),E=(1,0) paths from (0,0) to (n,mn) whose every prefix satisfies #N>=m#E and which have exactly k consecutive NE factors; nne(D) counts consecutive NNE factors, without cyclic counting. Then W^(m)_(n,k)(t)=(binom(n,k)/n)*sum_{j=1}^k binom(k,j)*binom(mn-k,j-1)*t^j. papers.title: The associative-commutative spectrum of SC229
papers.problem_definition: For A={0,1,2} with operation table rows (0,0,0), (1,0,1), (1,1,1), and every finite nonempty fixed label set I, two full linear binary terms on I (each variable once, arbitrary order, no constants) induce the same function A^I -> A if and only if their leftmost-decomposition trees agree as rooted labelled trees with exactly one distinguished child at each nonleaf and all other children unordered. Every such decorated tree is realised. Hence for every n>=1 the number c_n of these term functions is (n-1)! times the sum, for k=0,...,n-1, of binom(n,k) k^(n-1-k)/(n-1-k)!, with 0^0=1. Equivalently T(x)=sum_{n>=1}c_n x^n/n! satisfies T=x(1+T exp(T)); a direct integer recurrence and a function-only recursive decoder are supplied. This resolves the exact all-n counting question in source.md at its frozen interpretation in problem.md.

papers.title: Schur (2,2) reconstruction for explicit length classes
papers.problem_definition: Let n>=2 and c_j(n)=n*(n^2-1+3*2^(j-1)-3^j)/3. If c_j(n) is nonzero for every 1<=j<=n, then every n-element multiset of positive real numbers, including repetitions, is uniquely determined by the cardinality and first n logarithmic power sums of its complete Schur-(2,2) monomial-value multiset, with tableau multiplicities. This condition holds for every n>=3 with n!=4 and n modulo 60 outside {14,26,34,46}. Moreover, lengths 2 and 4 are uniquely reconstructible when the positive input sum is prescribed. Consequently, for every integer N>=2, positive integer partitions lambda,mu of N of length at least two and common length outside {14,26,34,46} modulo 60 satisfy S22(lambda)=S22(mu) only if lambda=mu. Equal output cardinalities force equal lengths. No converse, counterexample at an excluded length, or all-length resolution is claimed. Exact scope and proofs are Theorems A--C of evidence/research-moment-proof.md.

papers.title: All partition-restricted counts of nondegenerate 2 by 4 by 3 hypermatrices

papers.title: Quadratic positivity for finite-field q-hit residues

papers.title: Recurrent constant-term words for a degenerate Laurent polynomial
papers.problem_definition: For every prime p, set K=F_p and P(x)=x^(p-1)+x^(-1). For every Laurent polynomial Q in K[x,x^(-1)], define u_n=[x^0](P(x)^n Q(x)) for every integer n>=0. The condition in (iii) is the subspace P K[P], not the full Laurent-ring ideal. This covers all primes, including 2, zero Q, and arbitrary finite positive and negative Laurent exponents. It settles source.md for this specified P, without claiming a classification for other degenerate P or higher prime powers.

papers.title: Nonconvergence of the normalized size of the second remainder set

papers.title: A direct-sum law for the Ray–West correction and a statistic for separable permutations
papers.problem_definition: For every nonempty alpha in S_a and beta in S_b, let j(p)=(m^4+2m^3+m^2+4m+4)/2-g_2(p) for m=|p|, and let T(alpha), H(beta) indicate a decreasing last, respectively first, sum-indecomposable component, including singletons. Consequently j on every separable permutation equals the sum over maximal decomposition-tree nodes of adjacent decreasing-child pairs at sum nodes and adjacent increasing-child pairs at skew nodes. Among sum-decomposable permutations j(p)=|p|-1 if and only if p is layered; among skew-decomposable permutations equality holds if and only if p is colayered. No full-scope formula or equality classification is claimed for permutations indecomposable in both senses.

papers.title: A direct first-return enumeration of (2,2)-stack-sortable permutations
papers.problem_definition: For every integer n>=0, in the frozen (2,2)-stack input-sorting model of source.md and problem.md, the sortable permutations of [n] are in size-preserving bijection with the following canonical rank words: words with n pushes and n pops that start and end with an empty bit stack, obey P1: empty -> 0 and aT -> 1aT; P2: aT -> 10T; Q1: aT -> T; Q2: 0bT -> 0T, where a,b are bits and T is any suffix, and avoid the adjacent factor P2 Q1. papers.title: Higher-index failure of ultra-log-concavity for Chen's recursion polynomials
papers.problem_definition: For every integer m >= 4, let f_m(s)=((s+1)^m-(-1)^m)/(s+2) and h_m(s)=((s+1)^m+(-1)^m(s+1))/(s+2). For either P in {f_m,h_m}, write P(s)=sum_{j=0}^{m-1} a_j s^j. These are monic degree-(m-1) polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. For every integer j satisfying 4 <= j <= m-2, j(m-1-j)a_j^2 < (j+1)(m-j)a_{j-1}a_{j+1}. Moreover, for every m >= 4 the difference j(m-1-j)a_j^2-(j+1)(m-j)a_{j-1}a_{j+1} equals -m at j=m-2. Thus neither f_m nor h_m is ordinary ultra-log-concave, meaning that (a_j/binom(m-1,j)) is not log-concave, for any m >= 4. This includes both clauses of source.md and the m=4,5 cases with empty higher-index range.

papers.title: Positivity of one-sided fractional Gaussian noise predictors for five increments
papers.problem_definition: For every real H with 1/2<H<1, define rho_0(H)=1 and rho_j(H)=((j+1)^(2H)-2*j^(2H)+|j-1|^(2H))/2 for integers j>=1. papers.title: An explicit formal quotient for Class 214 inversion sequences

In formal series at z=0 define X=(1-2z-sqrt(1-4z))/(2z), with sqrt(1-4z)=1+O(z); q=X^2/(1+2X); b=X^3/((1+X)(1+2X)); H(u)=z(1+u)^2-u; R0(u)=-zu^2(1-z-zu)/(1-zu); R1(u)=u^2(1-z-zu)^2/(1-zu). For every j>=0 define t_j=z^j q/(1-q sum_{r=1}^j z^r), with the empty sum zero, and D_j=product_{i=0}^j H(t_i). Then A=sum_{j>=0}R0(t_j)/D_j and L=q+sum_{j>=0}R1(t_j)/D_j converge z-adically in Z[[z]], their summands having exact orders j+4 and j+3 respectively, and F=(b-A)/(zL). Here L=z^2+O(z^3) and b-A=z^3+O(z^4), so the quotient is well-defined. If A_m,L_m retain exactly j=0,...,m-1 and F_m=(b-A_m)/(zL_m), then for every integer m>=0, F_m belongs to Q(z,X) intersect Z[[z]] and F_m-F=z^(m+3)+O(z^(m+4)). papers.title: King on generalized staircases with equal odd blocks
papers.problem_definition: For every odd positive integer r and every positive integer k, let D_k be the nonempty partition consisting of r copies of kr, then r copies of (k-1)r, and so on down to r copies of r. A legal King move deletes its first row, its first column, or both, by exactly one unit, and is allowed only when the resulting partition is nonempty. Let G be its normal-play Sprague-Grundy value. If q is the unique integer with 0<=q<r+2 and q congruent to k modulo r+2, then G(D_k)=0 when q is odd, G(D_k)=1 when q is even and nonzero, and G(D_k)=2 when q=0. This is exactly the universal Conjecture 5.1 frozen in source.md, without restrictions to finite parameters or changes to empty-position conventions.

papers.title: Polynomial-time counting of two-level transpose fibres
papers.problem_definition: For every finite weakly increasing sequence C=(c_1,...,c_t) of positive integers that is 2-singleton (no repeated odd height), the number F_2(C) of Ferrers shapes B with l_2(B)=C, with leading zero columns identified and preimage width unrestricted, is computable in time polynomial in the binary input length log(t+1)+sum_i log(c_i+1). The empty target has count 1. For t>=1, put s_i=c_(t+1-i), s_(t+1)=0 and a_i=floor(s_i/2)-ceil(s_(i+1)/2). There is an explicit bijection between the fibre and integer vectors d>=0 satisfying d_i+d_(i+1)<=a_i for i<t and d_t<=a_t. More generally, for every nonnegative integer vector a of length t>=1, with A=max_i a_i, the proposed exact algorithm counts these vectors in O(t^4) integer arithmetic operations on O(t log(A+t+2))-bit integers and O(t^2) stored integers. Thus O(t^6 log^2(A+t+2)) elementary bit operations suffice. Its layer-i count function has at most i integer-interval polynomial pieces of degree at most i-1. The claim is restricted to m=2 and does not resolve the original arbitrary-m problem.

papers.title: A counterexample to multiset rook-Eulerian interlacing
papers.problem_definition: Under Definitions 5, 8, 9 and equations (10)--(12) of Alexandersson--Jal--Quemener, arXiv:2502.05939v1, take the non-skew Ferrers board lambda=(3,3,3,3,4,4) and content alpha=(2,2,1,1). There are exactly 60 legal words with strict adjacent ascents and no sentinel, and the first-entry refinements are R3=t(t^2+8t+3), R2=t(8t^2+15t+1), and R1=t^2(t+7)(2t+1). The sequence (R3,R2,R1) is not interlacing: its required ordered pair R3 preceq R1 fails because their degrees are 3 and 4 and minroot(R3)=-4-sqrt(13)<-7=minroot(R1). Thus the interlacing clause of Conjecture 28 is false, disproving the exact original conjunction frozen in source.md. This does not decide the separately quantified total real-rootedness clause. Indeed, all three refinements and the total R=2t(t^3+12t^2+15t+2) in this witness are real-rooted. No minimality or universal total-polynomial counterexample is asserted.

papers.title: Exact directional NFA separation for binary words with one marker
papers.problem_definition: Use epsilon-free NFAs over {0,1} with a finite nonempty state set, one initial state, an arbitrary accepting subset, and possibly missing transitions. Let nsep(w,x) be the minimum state count of an NFA accepting w and rejecting x, with unrestricted behavior on all other words. All word lengths are allowed and the maximum is attained. Consequently the unrestricted A(q) from source.md is at least (q-1)^2+2; its asymptotic growth remains unresolved.

papers.title: The shifted subtree-root annulus for trees of diameter at most three
papers.problem_definition: Let T be any finite simple tree of order n>=2 and diameter at most three, and let Phi_T(z)=sum_{k=1}^n s_k(T) z^k, where s_k(T) counts nonempty connected induced vertex subsets of cardinality k, each counted once. Every complex zero z of Phi_T satisfies 1/2<=|z+1/2|<=1/2+(n-1)^(1/(n-1)). The zero z=0 is simple and is the only zero on the inner boundary. A zero lies on the outer boundary if and only if n is even and T is the star K_{1,n-1}; in that case the unique outer-boundary zero is z=-1-(n-1)^(1/(n-1)). In particular, for every pair of integers a,b>=1, the double star D(a,b), obtained from an edge uv by attaching a leaves to u and b leaves to v, has all its nonzero subtree roots strictly between the two circles, with n=a+b+2. The frozen original claim for arbitrary trees, without a diameter restriction, remains unresolved.

papers.title: Conditional Schur positivity for binary-word events with at most four free positions
papers.problem_definition: For every n>=1, let a_n(A) count binary words of length n ending in 1 whose event set A consists exactly of the ending positions of factors 10 and 011. For every J subset of {2,...,n} with m=|J|<=4 and every S subset of {2,...,n}\J, the homogeneous symmetric polynomial H_(S,J)(x,y)=sum_(T subset J) a_n(S union T) a_n(S union (J\T)) x^|T| y^(m-|T|) is Schur-positive in two variables. Thus, if G(t;z)=sum_(T subset J) a_n(S union T)t^|T| product_(i in T) z_i=sum_k g_k(z)t^k, every g_k(z)^2-g_(k-1)(z)g_(k+1)(z) is coefficientwise nonnegative, with g_k=0 outside its range. There is no bound on n, the spacing of J, or |S|; all other event indicators are fixed, and zero-count cases are included. The two-position inequality a_n(S)a_n(S union {i,j})<=2a_n(S union {i})a_n(S union {j}) has optimal factor 2, attained at n=4,S=empty,{i,j}={2,4}. The pair-polynomial conclusion also holds for arbitrary |J| when J can be partitioned in its natural order into blocks of at most four positions such that, between each consecutive pair of blocks, S contains two adjacent positions. No unrestricted weighted theorem, full exceptional-class log-concavity, or resolution of the original 21-family assertion is claimed.

papers.title: Positive initial coefficients and a positivity region for Brugidou's hook polynomials
papers.problem_definition: Let phi_q(e_j)=q^(j(j-1)/2)/j! and define J_lambda by phi_q(m_lambda)=(1-q)^(n-r) q^nu(lambda) J_lambda/((n-1)! product_j a_j(lambda)!), where n=|lambda|, r=l(lambda), nu(lambda)=sum_i(i-1)lambda_i and a_j(lambda) is the multiplicity of j. For all integers a>=2,b>=0, set K_(a,b)=J_(a,1^b)/b!, d=binom(a-1,2)+(a-1)b and D=binom(a-2,2). Then K_(a,b) is in Z[q], and [q^k]K_(a,b)>0 for every integer 0<=k<=min(d,2b+3). If b>=max(0,ceil((D-4)/2)), every coefficient from degree 0 through d is strictly positive. With the established one-row cases b=0, this covers all hooks with 2<=a<=6. No assertion of optimality, log-concavity, or full all-partition positivity is made.

papers.title: A compositional inverse for the support polynomials of comb preorder polytopes
papers.problem_definition: Let tau_0 be empty, and for every integer n>=0 obtain tau_(n+1) by taking the disjoint union of tau_n with a singleton and then adjoining a new minimum. Let Q_n consist of the nonnegative real vectors on the 2n vertices satisfying sum_(v in I) x_v <= |I| for every lower ideal I of tau_n, and let h_n(t)=sum_(a in Q_n intersect Z^(2n)) t^(number of positive coordinates of a), with h_0(t)=1. For an indeterminate t, define F(t,x)=sum_(n>=0) t^(-n) h_n(t) x^(n+1) and R(t,x)=sum_(m>=1) (-1)^(m-1) [1+(1+t)^m t^(1-m) sum_(j=0)^(m-2) t^j] x^m, where the inner sum is zero for m=1. Then R(t,F(t,x))=x=F(t,R(t,x)) in Q(t)[[x]]. Equivalently, the same R is x/[(1+x)(1+(1+t)x)(1+(1+t)x/t)] and is the compositional inverse of the full support-refined comb generating series. This is the entire identity frozen in source.md, with no restriction to a finite range or scalar specialization of t.

papers.title: Singular energy minima and fixed-product structure for all-odd complex unit gain dumbbells
papers.problem_definition: For every odd r,s>=3 and odd ell>=1, use the frozen graph and normalized gain real parts alpha,beta of problem.md, and put L=(ell-1)/2, N=r+s+ell-1, H=(s+L)alpha+(r+L)beta. The Hermitian characteristic polynomial satisfies P(0)=(-1)^(N/2)(1-4alpha beta) and P_x(0)=-2(-1)^(N/2)H. Thus its zero eigenvalue exists exactly on alpha beta=1/4 and is simple throughout that locus in the closed square. At each interior point q of that locus, with Z,W,X,Y the source Lemma 4.2 polynomials, A=Z-alpha beta W, B=alpha X+beta Y, C=A^2+B^2, I_alpha=integral_0^infinity(-beta WA+XB)/(t^2 C)dt, and I_beta=integral_0^infinity(-alpha WA+YB)/(t^2 C)dt, one has E(q+h)=E(q)+(2/pi)(I_alpha h_alpha+I_beta h_beta)+2|beta h_alpha+alpha h_beta|/|H|+O(||h||^2). Therefore a necessary condition for an interior singular local minimum is alpha I_alpha=beta I_beta and |alpha I_alpha+beta I_beta|<=pi/(2|H|); together with strict inequality these conditions suffice for a strict local minimum. Equality in the normal bound is unclassified. Away from the singular locus the usual necessary interior conditions I_alpha=I_beta=0 hold. For every 0<p<1 the energy on alpha beta=p in the positive square is strictly convex in u=(1/2)log(alpha/beta), hence has a unique constrained minimum; at p=1 the curve is a singleton. When r=s the constrained minimum is (sqrt(p),sqrt(p)). When r<s its coordinates satisfy alpha<beta for p<1, and X(t)/Y(t)>(s+L)/(r+L) for all t>0. In particular, if p>=(r+L)/(s+L) the constrained minimum is exactly (p,1); if s+L>=4(r+L), the unique positive singular-curve minimum is (1/4,1) and there is no interior singular local minimum. Exchange of cycles and simultaneous negation give the corresponding statements. These constrained endpoint minima are not asserted to minimize the full square. For D_(3,3,1), the full-square minima are exactly (+1/2,+1/2) and (-1/2,-1/2), with eight oriented cycle-gain switching lifts and common energy 2+sqrt(13)+sqrt(5); the source equation (117) integrals at the positive minimizer are strictly positive, while its diagonal derivative jump is 4/3. For D_(3,3,5), exact root intervals put the directional energy derivative at (1/2,1/2) along (-1,-1) strictly between -8/1000 and -7/1000, so this singular point is not a local minimum. Complete arguments and all scope exclusions are in evidence/singular-branch.md. The full original all-odd global minimum/equality classification remains unresolved.

papers.title: A Narayana factorization for a truncated two-row grid polytope
papers.problem_definition: For every integer n>=1, let P_n=({1,...,n} x {1,2}) minus {(n,2)}, ordered coordinatewise, and Q_n={x>=0: sum_{v in I}x_v<=|I| for every lower ideal I of P_n}. Then sum_{x in Q_n intersect Z^(2n-1)} t^(number of nonzero coordinates of x) equals A_{n-1}(t) B_n(t), where A_r(t)=sum_{j=0}^r binom(r,j)binom(r+1,j)t^j/(j+1) and B_r(t)=sum_{j=0}^r binom(r,j)^2 t^j. This is the entire frozen original claim, with no change of statistic, hypotheses, or parameter range.

papers.title: A two-step bound for the modes of uniform hypercomb summands
papers.problem_definition: For every pair of integers n>=2 and ell>=3, let a=(1+(ell-2)x)(1+(ell-1)x), b=x(1+(ell-1)x), z0=1+ell*x, z1=(1+(ell-1)x)(a+2*x), F0=0, F1=1, and Fj=a*F_(j-1)+b*F_(j-2) for j>=2. Set Wn=z1*Fn and Yn=z0*b*F_(n-1), the Galvin-Sharpe Section 2.5 decomposition Cn=Wn+Yn. With zero-extended coefficients define P<=_lr Q by p_i*q_j>=p_j*q_i for all integers i<j. Then Wn<=_lr x^2*Yn and Yn<=_lr x*Wn. Hence the smallest coefficient-maximizing indices satisfy m(Yn)-1<=m(Wn)<=m(Yn)+2. In particular, Cn is nondecreasing up to r=min(m(Wn),m(Yn)) and nonincreasing from q=max(m(Wn),m(Yn)), where q-r<=2. The summand separation bound two is attained by unique modes 6 and 4 at n=3,ell=5. Full unimodality and log-concavity of Cn for all parameters remain unproved here.

papers.title: Quadratic standard monomials for fixed involution classes
papers.problem_definition: For every n>0 and 0<=a<=n with a congruent to n modulo 2, a>=2, and k=(n-a)/2>=2, let H_n be all squarefree two-edge matching monomials in off-diagonal variables y_ij, i<j, and let T_n={y_12*y_ij:3<=i<j<=n} union {y_13*y_2j:4<=j<=n} union {y_1j*y_23:4<=j<=n} union {y_15*y_24,y_15*y_34,y_25*y_34}. The literal Pieri-RSK candidate specified in problem.md in degree 2 equals H_n minus T_n and is a basis of R(M_(n,a))_2. For the presentation Q[y_ij]/ker(y_ij maps to [x_ij]), or its scalar extension to C, H_n minus T_n is its degree-2 standard monomial set for every monomial order refining the positive variable weights n^2-ij. Every t in T_n has a unique homogeneous straightening into H_n minus T_n, and a nonzero coefficient at h implies sum_(ij in t) ij < sum_(ij in h) ij. Degrees 0 and 1 have the literal candidate and standard monomial sets {1} and {y_ij:(i,j)!=(1,2)}. Consequently, for every n>=6 their union is a complete explicit standard monomial basis of R(M_(n,n-4)), with Hilbert series 1+(C(n,2)-1)q+(3*C(n,4)-C(n,2))q^2. No universal higher-degree assertion or complete resolution of original Problem 29 is claimed.

papers.title: Sharp connection-Dirac spectral-sum domination for graph complexes
papers.problem_definition: For every nonempty finite abstract simplicial complex G whose faces all have cardinality at most two, let L_G be the unweighted face-intersection matrix and D_G the unaugmented oriented-incidence Dirac matrix defined in problem.md. For every integer 1 <= k <= |G|, S_k(L_G) >= S_k(D_G) + 1, where S_k sums the k largest eigenvalues with multiplicity. The constant 1 is sharp, already at k=1 for the complex consisting of one edge and its two vertices. Disconnected complexes, isolated vertices, and non-bipartite graphs are included. This is only the dimension-at-most-one case; the original arbitrary-dimensional comparison remains unresolved.

papers.title: Two-vertex cuts and a Lorentzian obstruction for bistable bipartite graphs
papers.problem_definition: For every integer k>=2 and every finite connected simple bipartite graph F with parts L,R of size k whose only maximum independent sets are L and R, set A=[[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,1]], f=Z_(F,A) with the unnormalized labeled-assignment convention in problem.md, beta=(k-1,k-1,0), and c=[x1^(k-1)x2^(k-1)x3^2]f. For distinct u,v let q(u,v) be the number of connected components of F-{u,v}, including isolated vertices; let s count unordered pairs within L or within R for which q(u,v)>1. Then c=sum_(u in L,v in R)2^q(u,v)+2s and Hessian(partial^beta f)=2(k!)^2 [[0,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,c/k^2]]. In particular c>=2k^2, with equality exactly when F has no two-vertex cut. Such F is 2-connected. The selected Hessian has two positive eigenvalues exactly when F is not 3-connected, proving that f is not Lorentzian in that case; A is admissible with spectrum -1,1-sqrt(2),1+sqrt(2). If F is 3-connected this Hessian has one positive, one negative, and one zero eigenvalue, without any assertion that f itself is Lorentzian. Corollaries: c=6k(k-1) for C_(2k), k>=2; c=2k^2 for K_(k,k), k>=3; c=12 for K_(2,2)=C4. The original universal connected-clique characterization remains unresolved.

papers.title: A zero-free disk for the minimum cost of a four-edge bipartite matching
papers.problem_definition: For every pair of integers m,n>=4, assign independent rate-one exponential costs to the edges of K_{m,n}, and let C_{4,m,n} be the minimum total cost of a matching of four edges. Then F_{4,m,n}(t)=E exp(t C_{4,m,n}) is nonzero for every complex t with |t|<mn/4. Moreover, every zero of the reduced numerator of its rational continuation has modulus strictly greater than mn/4. The proof establishes the stronger algebraic statement that the explicit sextic P_{m,n} in evidence/k4-proof.md has no root in |t|<=mn/4 for all real m,n>=4, using F_{4,m,n}=A P_{m,n}/Q for integer parameters. Boundary poles are not claimed to be finite nonzero values. The frozen conjecture for unrestricted k remains unresolved.

papers.title: Sharp local-dimension jumps and degree-jump growth in the partition graph
papers.problem_definition: For the simple undirected unit-transfer graph on all integer partitions of n defined in source.md and problem.md, with d the degree and delta the largest clique containing a vertex minus one: for every integer n>=2, D_delta(n) is 0 for n=2,3, is 1 for 4<=n<=10 and n=12,13, and is 2 for n=11 and all n>=14. For every integer n>=10, put T_s=s(s+1)/2 and choose the unique s with T_s<=n<T_(s+1). Then 4s-8<=D_d(n)<=4s+2, and consequently D_d(n)=4sqrt(2n)+O(1) with an absolute error bound as n tends to infinity. Lower witnesses exist for every n in the claimed ranges. Also orient any edge lambda->mu toward nondecreasing support and let k=r(mu)-r(lambda). Define H(v) to mean that some positive size x>=2 occurs at least twice in v while x-1 is absent. The edge has absolute dimension jump two if and only if either k=1, lambda is neither a staircase nor H and mu is H, or k=2 and both endpoints are H. The separate qualitative localization question in source Problem 8.2 is not asserted resolved; no exact formula for D_d beyond these bounds is asserted.

papers.title: A counterexample to distributivity of fixed pinnacle-order fibers
papers.problem_definition: Let P_5((5)) be all permutations of [5] whose complete left-to-right list of interior pinnacle values is exactly (5), with endpoints excluded from peaks. Order this fiber by coordinatewise comparison of I_v(pi), the number of values smaller than v to the right of v. This nonempty induced poset is not a distributive lattice. An exact witness consists of e=12354, b=12534, a=13524, c=13452, d=13542. All five lie in the fiber, and their meets and joins computed among every element of the fiber satisfy b join c=d, a meet d=a, a meet b=b, a meet c=e, b join e=b, with a different from b. Thus a meet (b join c) differs from (a meet b) join (a meet c). This disproves the universal assertion asked in Liang--Sagan Question 8.6(a) in the published version, equivalently Question 8.7(a) of arXiv:2408.02782v1, including its explicitly qualified nonempty-fiber version. No assertion about counting part (b), minimality in n, or a classification of other fibers is submitted.

papers.title: A two-factor criterion for unimodality of stretched q-integer products
papers.problem_definition: For every integer r>=2 and all positive integers a,c,b, define [a]_q=sum_{i=0}^{a-1}q^i and [b]_(q^r)=sum_{j=0}^{b-1}q^(rj). The full integer-indexed coefficient sequence of [a]_q[c]_q[b]_(q^r), including zero coefficients, is weakly unimodal if and only if r divides a, or r divides c, or b<=1+floor(a/r)+floor(c/r). The disjunction is inclusive and factor-1 cases are included. This is exactly the k=2 restriction of the original Conjecture 5.4; no assertion resolving its other parameter ranges is submitted.

papers.title: The log-concavity to log-convexity transition in fixed columns of Stirling numbers
papers.problem_definition: Let c(n,k) count permutations of n elements with k cycles, with c(0,0)=1 and c(n,k)=0 outside 0<=k<=n. For each integer k>=1 there exists an integer N_k>=k+1 such that D_k(n)=c(n,k)^2-c(n-1,k)c(n+1,k) is nonnegative for every integer 1<=n<N_k and strictly negative for every integer n>=N_k. Hence the full weak-inequality assertion frozen in source.md holds. The proof establishes the sufficient inequality q_k(n)-2q_k(n+1)+q_k(n+2)>=0 for every n>=k>=1, where q_k(n)=c(n,k-1)/c(n,k); it is strict for k>=2 and an equality for k=1. An admissible finite threshold is N_k=1+min{j>=k:q_k(j)-q_k(j+1)<1}.

papers.title: Simple negative roots for the rows of the Delannoy matrix square
papers.problem_definition: Let D(n,k) count paths from (0,0) to (n-k,k) using steps (1,0), (0,1), and (1,1), with D(n,k)=0 outside 0<=k<=n and the empty path counted once. For the ordinary matrix square define G_n(x)=sum_{k=0}^n sum_{i=k}^n D(n,i)D(i,k)x^k. Then G_0=1, and for every integer n>=1, G_n is monic of degree n and has n distinct real roots, all in the open interval (-4-3*sqrt(2), -3+2*sqrt(2)). This claim concerns only D^2; it does not assert the A^2 part of the frozen original or consecutive interlacing.

papers.title: Interval shape and endpoint collisions for totally positive shifted even powers
papers.problem_definition: For every even integer n>=2, for the sets M_n defined verbatim in source.md and precisely in problem.md, there exists c_n with M_n=[-c_n,1+c_n] and (sqrt(2)-1)/2<=c_n<1-1/sqrt(2). At t=-c_n, Q_(n,t) has exactly one double zero r in (-1,0), all other zeros are simple and smaller than r, partial_z^2 Q_(n,t)(r)>0, and partial_t Q_(n,t)(r)<0; the other endpoint has the reflected configuration. The proof establishes the following operator theorem: if -3/10<=t<0, h has even degree d>=2, positive leading coefficient, and d simple zeros in (-1,0), S=h'(0)/h(0), delta=(1+2t)/(1+t)^2, and 0<lambda<=1/(S+delta), then T_t^2[(z-lambda)h] has d+2 simple zeros in (-1,0) and one simple positive zero, where T_t p=z(1+z)p'+(z+t)p. Equality in the lambda bound is included. Consequently every odd Q_(m,t), m>=1, has m-1 simple zeros in (-1,0) and one simple positive zero for -3/10<=t<0. The original successive-nesting assertion c_n<=c_(n+2) is not claimed and remains unresolved.

papers.title: An Ehrhart–word identity for arbor polytopes
papers.contribution: For every integer n>=1, every partition of [n] into nonempty blocks B_v, and every rooted tree tau on those blocks, let D_v be the union of descendant blocks including B_v and N_v=|D_v|. Set Q_tau={x in R^n: x_i>=0 for all i and sum_{i in D_v} x_i<=N_v for every v}. Let W_tau be all length-n words over [n] with at least N_v occurrences of letters from D_v for every v, and des(w)=|{j:1<=j<n, w_j>w_{j+1}}|. With sum_{m>=0}|m Q_tau intersect Z^n| t^m=h*(Q_tau,t)/(1-t)^(n+1), one has h*(Q_tau,t)=sum_{w in W_tau} t^(n-1-des(w)). Equivalently, for every integer m>=0, |m Q_tau intersect Z^n|=sum_{a in A_tau} product_{i=1}^n binom(m+1,a_i), where A_tau={a in Z_{≥0}^n:sum_i a_i=n and sum_{i in D_v} a_i>=N_v for every v}, and binom(m+1,a_i)=0 when a_i>m+1. No restriction on block labels, sizes, depth, or branching is imposed.

papers.title: Whirling knight's tours with n coils and with the least number of coils
papers.contribution: Knuth's exercise 7.2.2.4-231 (TAOCP Pre-Fascicle 8A, draft of 8 May 2026) asks for n x n whirling knight's tours with exactly n/2 coils and with exactly n coils. (1) n coils: for every n >= 5 with n not divisible by 4, no such tour exists (weighted counting argument); new tours for n = 16, 20, 24; with the constructions and counts reported in Knuth's draft, a tour with n coils exists if and only if n = 3, or n >= 12 and 4 | n. (2) Lower bound: every tour has at least n/2 + 2 coils when n = 4 or 6 (mod 8), and at least (n+3)/2 coils when n >= 5 is odd and not congruent to 1 or 19 (mod 24); the proof bounds the number of disjoint paths needed to cover a wedge of the board by an explicit labelling, and for n = 4, 6 (mod 8) it contains S. Li's theorem that n/2 coils are impossible. (3) For every n >= 11 the least number of coils is determined: n/2 if n = 0, 2 (mod 8), n/2 + 2 if n = 4, 6 (mod 8), (n+1)/2 if n = 1, 19 (mod 24), (n+3)/2 for the other odd n. The tours: explicit ones for small n, and for larger n nested rings of width 12 built from twenty-four seed tours whose ring can be stretched by inserting periods (computer-assisted: a lemma on inserting a period into a system of disjoint paths plus finite conditions on the seeds). Hence a tour with n/2 coils exists if and only if n >= 16 and n = 0 or 2 (mod 8). (4) For n = 3 (mod 4) no ring that replaces a single arc was found; the six seeds for this case replace 28 to 31 short pieces of the inner tour, in its five outer layers, by paths with the same ends that between them pass through all cells of the ring. (5) Rotational symmetry: a whirling tour invariant under the half turn has an odd number of coils, and one invariant under the quarter turn exists only if 4 does not divide n; for every n >= 11 the least number of coils of a tour with half-turn symmetry is the least odd number that is at least the overall minimum, and it is attained with quarter-turn symmetry when 4 does not divide n. (6) The greatest number of coils is n if 4 | n and n - 1 otherwise, for every n >= 10; the tours are nests of rings that add 24 coils each, which also gives a construction of tours with n coils independent of the one in Knuth's draft. With half-turn symmetry the greatest number of coils is n - 1 for even n and n - 2 for odd n. (7) For every n >= 6, every number of coils between the least and the greatest one occurs, so the numbers of coils form an interval that is known for every n. (8) The same for tours with rotational symmetry: every odd number between the least and the greatest one occurs. (9) A ring of width 12 that replaces one arc adds at least 14 coils when n = 3 (mod 4), so the multi-piece rings are necessary there.

papers.title: Closed knight's tours with 7.5 n + O(1) crossings
papers.contribution: Knuth's exercise 7.2.2.4-161 (TAOCP Pre-Fascicle 8A, draft of 8 May 2026) asks whether a closed n x n knight's tour can have fewer than 12n + O(1) crossings, the number in the construction of Besa, Johnson, Mamano, Osegueda and Williams, who also prove that 4n - O(1) are necessary. Theorem: for every even n >= 30 there is a closed knight's tour of the n x n board with exactly 7.5 n + 13 crossings. The tours are explicit: one field of parallel moves in the interior, four periodic wall patterns, and 179 cells near the corners and near the middle of one wall, taken once and for all from a tour of side 40 found by a solver. Computer-assisted: the paper lists all joins between the 3n - 32 lines of the field (fourteen exceptional joins and five arithmetic rules), checked by a program for 30 <= n <= 54 and proved for larger n from the periodicity of the patterns; that the joins form a single cycle is then proved directly from the list. A variant with 43n/6 + 24 crossings is checked for n = 48, 60, ..., 600 only.

papers.title: How many edges can be removed from a flower snark line graph?
papers.contribution: Knuth's exercise 7.2.2.3-233 (TAOCP Volume 4, Fascicle 7, 2025) asks how many edges can be removed from the line graph L(J_q) of the flower snark J_q, q odd, before it becomes 3-colorable; his answer hopes for a reader's answer and reports nine. Theorem: for every odd q >= 5 the maximum is exactly 9, and the removable 9-edge sets are exactly the 4q claw sets (the edges of L(J_q) touching the three edges of J_q at one vertex); for q = 3 the maximum is 15 (unique). For q >= 7 the number of removable k-edge sets is q times 12, 132, 324, 498, 504, 336, 144, 36, 4 (k = 1..9). Lower bound by the parity lemma (for every snark); upper bound computer-assisted by a 27-state Boolean transfer matrix with T^2 = T^4.

papers.title: The largest removable edge sets of the pinched Sierpinski gasket
papers.contribution: Knuth's exercise 7.2.2.3-227 (TAOCP Volume 4, Fascicle 7, 2025) asks for the largest number of edges removable from the pinched Sierpinski gasket (corners 0^n and 1^n identified) before it becomes 3-colourable; the answer gives Filip Stappers' 2^(n-1) sets of 2^(n-1)+1 edges and asks whether they are all the largest sets for every n (known for n <= 4). Theorem: yes, for every n >= 2. Proof: an exact recursion over the corner colour patterns of a gasket (15 profiles), closed forms for all profiles by an induction reduced to a finite computation, and the maximizing terms of the recursion reproduce Stappers' refinement rule.

papers.title: Three remarks on TAOCP Pre-Fascicle 8A: exercises 157(b), 204(b) and 205
papers.contribution: Three remarks on Knuth's draft of TAOCP Section 7.2.2.4 (Pre-Fascicle 8A, 8 May 2026). (1) Answer 157(b) says no explanation is known for the absence of closed 8x8 knight's tours with at least two moves in every one of the 21 symmetry classes; in fact five classes (D, I, K, L, N) always carry exactly eight moves, because each of the eight cells next to a corner spends one move on its corner and its other move in these classes. (2) The field count in the trie-building loop of answer 204(b) has its two cases interchanged (confirmed by running the loop literally). (3) The case n = 1 of research problem 205: exact average number of pointers for one random key, and its expansion q^2/6 - q^{3/2}/3 + 7q/2 - c sqrt q + O(1).

papers.title: A fully clued Slitherlink diagram with exactly five solutions
papers.contribution: Answers the question Knuth added in 2023 to the answer of TAOCP exercise 7.2.2.1-411 ('It's currently unknown whether or not exactly five loops are possible'): a fully clued 13x13 Slitherlink diagram with exactly five solutions. Also fully clued 12x12 and 13x13 diagrams with exactly six, answering Beluhov's question (arXiv:2308.08798, Sec. 10) whether multiplicity >= 5 is possible, and exhaustive searches showing that every fully clued diagram with fewer than 144 cells has at most four solutions.
